name: Ehrwalder Alm
kurzbeschreibung: The Ehrwalder Alm at 1,502 metres in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena is a beloved alpine plateau featuring rustic mountain huts, access to Lake Seebensee, and Zugspitze vistas.
preis: Pasture trails freely accessible; Ehrwalder Almbahn gondola charges apply
oeffnungszeiten: Gondola operates daily from late May to early November
beschreibung:
Überblick

The Ehrwalder Alm rests at an elevation of 1,502 metres upon a sunlit mountain terrace cradled between the formidable Wetterstein mountain range and the jagged Mieming Chain in the Tiroler Zugspitz Arena. Cherished as one of the most scenic and accessible alpine excursion destinations in Western Tirol, the plateau combines verdant dairy pastures with dramatic limestone precipices. Directly above the green meadows, the sheer vertical walls of Germany's and Austria's border peaks—including the iconic Zugspitze and the sharp pyramid of the Sonnenspitze—dominate the horizon. A constellation of authentic mountain chalets and alpine dairy huts welcome visitors with artisan cheeses, crisp strudels, and panoramic sundecks. Whether serving as a leisurely retreat for multigenerational families or as the launchpad for high-alpine hikes toward crystalline glacier-fed tarns, the Ehrwalder Alm delivers quintessentially authentic Tyrolean mountain magic.

Route & Anforderungen

Ascending to the Ehrwalder Alm is made effortless and barrier-free by the modern 8-seater Ehrwalder Almbahn gondola (approx. 8 minutes ride). Hikers preferring to ascend on foot can follow the wide paved forest road or the meadow footpaths from the valley station in roughly 1.5 hours (approx. 400 vertical metres). The plateau itself features a broad network of stroller-friendly paths and gentle loop trails. A world-renowned excursion leads from the mountain station along a graded alpine trail to Lake Seebensee (approx. 2 hours walking time, 250 metres ascent), frequently hailed as one of the most breathtaking alpine lakes in the Alps. Comfortable sneakers suffice around the top station, whereas ankle-high trekking boots with vibram rubber lugs are mandatory for the hike to Lake Seebensee and the Coburger Hütte refuge.

Besuch & Anreise

Road travel from the north is toll-free via Garmisch-Partenkirchen or Füssen/Reutte along highways B187 and B179 to Ehrwald. Generous free parking is available right at the Ehrwalder Almbahn valley gondola terminal. Rail passengers take the Außerfernbahn train to Ehrwald Zugspitzbahn station and board complimentary local guest shuttles directly to the lift base.

Tipps

Begin your trek toward Lake Seebensee early in the morning when the crystal waters remain mirror-calm: the reflection of the pyramid-shaped Sonnenspitze upon the turquoise mountain lake is one of the most celebrated photographic compositions in all of Europe.
